problems.source_says: The paper names no analysis unit for purchase intent, and Figure 8 rules out single ratings. The figure's 95 percent CI half-widths, read from the PDF's vector paths, run from 0.089 to 0.123 on the 1-7 scale. With the SDs printed on p. 13 (0.49 to 0.62), those widths imply about 97 to 154 observations per arm and about 640 to 650 in total, which is one mean per idea. The 320 raters each rated 20 ideas (6,400 ratings, about 1,067 per arm), and rating-level statistics would give half-widths near 0.03. The printed statistics are idea-level means, so the unit is output. S2-O1 is rightly coded rating, because its mixed models have one row per rating.
problems.quote: Mean purchase intent ratings with 95% confidence intervals across five conditions (scale: 1–7).
problems.locator: p. 27, Figure 8 (caption and error bars); p. 13, Section 6.3; p. 11, Sections 6.1-6.2

problems.source_says: The paper builds one quality score for each idea, and the linear model has one row per idea (one scored idea per person, t(481)). The form-spec rule for unit says that one row per idea is output, even when ideas are nested in people. The form codes the same structure as output with n_units 486 for S1-O2. No statistic changes, because each person has one scored idea.
problems.quote: For each idea, we averaged the originality and usefulness ratings across all raters to obtain a single idea quality score.
problems.locator: p. 7, Section 4.4; p. 22, Appendix D (judge only the first idea); form-spec.md, Field notes, unit

problems.form_value: Across coded ideas, elaboration depth correlated with idea diversity (r = 0.28, p = .032) but not with quality or ownership (both p > .15).
problems.source_says: The numbers match the text, but the paper does not say how many coded ideas entered the correlation. 'Across coded ideas' implies all 80. At n = 80, r = 0.28 gives a two-sided p of .012. The printed p = .032 fits about 59 observations, so the test may have used fewer than the 80 coded ideas. The gloss has no support in the text.
problems.quote: we correlated elaboration depth with our dependent variables. Results showed that deeper elaboration was associated with greater idea diversity (r = 0.28, p = .032), but not with quality or ownership (both p > .15).
problems.locator: p. 10, Section 5.4; p. 9, Section 5.4 (80 ideas in total)

confirmed.statement: Criterion 3 holds. In S1-O1, four domain experts from the innovation department of an automotive manufacturer rated every submitted idea for originality and usefulness on 7-point scales (CAT). The two ratings were averaged across raters, ICC(3,k) = .60. The score is not self-reported, and measure expert_raters fits.

S1-O2 is a computed measure on the submitted ideas: the cosine distance of each idea's text-embedding-3-large embedding to the leave-one-out centroid of the other ideas in its condition. It compares different people's ideas, so construct diversity fits. Higher values mean more diverse, which matches the signs in Tables 3 and 15.
confirmed.locator: p. 7, Section 4.4; p. 8, footnote 2; p. 12, Tables 2-3; p. 25, Table 15

confirmed.statement: AI was available when the scored final idea was written in all four Study 1 AI arms. Participants wrote an initial idea without AI, worked with GPT-4.1, and then refined and submitted. The suggestion-mode refinement box sits below the AI suggestions. The control had no LLM. So ai_available_when_produced yes fits S1-O1, S1-O2, and S1-O4.
confirmed.locator: p. 5, Section 4.1; pp. 6-7, Section 4.2; p. 6, Figure 2

confirmed.statement: S1-O3 compares initial ideas written without AI with refined ideas written with AI. Both are measured against the centroid of the condition's initial ideas, so mixed fits. The measure compares each idea with other people's initial ideas, so diversity (not flexibility) is right. The before-after rows are not randomized, as the form notes.
confirmed.locator: p. 8, Section 5.3 and footnote 2; p. 10, Figure 6; p. 24, Table 12 notes

summary: Criterion 3 holds, because Study 1's expert-rated quality and embedding diversity are scored on the ideas that participants submitted with GPT-4.1 available, and every printed number, question code, and construct in the outcome entries matches the PDF. The coding is still refuted on details: S2-O3 purchase intent is coded unit rating although Figure 8's error bars imply one mean per idea, S1-O1 is coded participant against the form-spec rule that one row per idea is output, and three smaller items need fixes (an unsupported 'across coded ideas' gloss and two statistics_available tags).
